CURRICULUM VITAE

Tomislav Mesarić
Ulica Lipa 12, 10000 Zagreb, Croatia | +385 1 555 0142 | tomislav.mesaric@example.com

PROFESSIONAL PROFILE
Butcher and meat-counter professional with experience since 2015 in carcass breakdown, boning, trimming, portioning and customer service. Experienced in advising customers on cuts and preparation, producing fresh sausages, rotating stock using FIFO, and maintaining cold-chain temperature and hygiene checks. Completed vocational butcher training and holds a renewed basic HACCP certificate.

KEY SKILLS
Carcass breakdown (beef, pork and lamb) · Boning, trimming and portioning · Fresh sausage production · Customer advice on cuts and preparation · FIFO stock rotation · Cold-chain temperature checks · HACCP and hygiene routines · Knife sharpening · Mincer and bandsaw operation · Cash handling

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Butcher | Mesnica Kod Ante (family butcher shop), Zagreb | 2019–present
- Break down 2–3 beef forequarters and 10–12 pork sides each week; bone, trim and portion meat for the counter.
- Make four kinds of fresh sausage to the shop’s recipes: ćevapi, kobasice, chipolata and lamb merguez. Produce about 40 kg weekly in the busy season.
- Developed the shop’s lamb merguez recipe and adjusted the ćevapi mix to 70% beef / 30% lamb in response to customer feedback. The ćevapi won second place at the Zagreb County craft meat fair in 2023.
- Record cold-room (0–4 °C) and display-counter temperature checks twice daily; rotate cold-room stock every morning using FIFO.
- Serve around 120 customers on a Saturday, advising on cuts and cooking times.
- Trained two apprentices in knife handling and cleaning routines.
- Prepared whole lambs and suckling pigs for spit-roasting at weddings and family events, including a 2024 wedding order for four lambs and two pigs serving 180 guests.
- Ran a six-week dry-ageing trial on beef ribs, recording temperatures and weight loss; the shop now sells dry-aged rib by pre-order.

Counter Assistant | Tržnica Dolac meat hall stall, Zagreb | 2015–2019
- Served customers, weighed and priced orders, operated the till and completed cash-up.
- Cleaned and sanitised slicers, mincers and the counter at closing.
- Created a closing and cleaning checklist for equipment and work areas following a market hygiene inspection remark; it remains in use at the stall.

EDUCATION & CERTIFICATES
Vocational Certificate: Butcher (3-year programme) | Food Trades School Zagreb | 2015
HACCP Basic Food Hygiene Certificate | 2021; renewed 2024
Preparing for the Master Butcher exam (majstorski ispit), planned for spring 2027; not yet passed

LANGUAGES
Croatian (native) · English (good; customer communication) · German (basic)


COVER LETTER

Dear Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Butcher / Meat Counter Assistant position at FreshCart Supermarkets’ Zagreb-Jarun store. I completed vocational butcher training and have worked in butchery and meat-counter roles since 2015, combining practical meat preparation with attentive customer service.

In my current role at Mesnica Kod Ante, I break down beef and pork, bone, trim and portion meat, and prepare fresh sausages. I also rotate cold-room stock each morning using FIFO and record cold-room and display-counter temperatures twice daily. At the counter, I serve around 120 customers on a Saturday and advise them on suitable cuts and cooking times. These responsibilities align closely with your need for careful stock rotation, hygiene checks and helpful, knowledgeable service.

I value the practical craft of butchery and the customer connection that comes with giving clear advice. FreshCart’s focus on fresh food and honest product guidance reflects the kind of service I aim to provide. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience and reliability to your meat-counter team.

Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to discussing how my experience could contribute to the Zagreb-Jarun store.

Kind regards,
Tomislav Mesarić

critique.content_quality_feedback: The actual letter is concise, professional, and clearly explains the candidate’s relevant butcher and meat-counter experience. It uses credible evidence, including carcass breakdown, sausage production, FIFO rotation, temperature records, and serving approximately 120 customers on Saturdays. However, the document begins with a complete CV and the heading “CURRICULUM VITAE” before the cover letter. This creates a confusing, unnecessarily long application document and obscures the intended letter. The letter also does not explicitly mention the candidate’s HACCP certificate or use the term “HACCP knowledge,” despite this being a stated requirement.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The cover letter itself uses simple headings, standard paragraph formatting, and job-relevant terminology that should parse well. The duplicated CV contains additional useful keywords, but including a full CV inside a document identified as a cover letter may confuse document classification and AI screening. The letter includes terms such as “break down,” “bone,” “trim,” “portion,” “fresh sausages,” “FIFO,” “temperature,” “customers,” and “cuts and cooking times.” It should explicitly include “HACCP” and “HACCP knowledge” to improve matching with the must-have requirement. AI screening probability is moderate to high for the core butcher and customer-service requirements, but is reduced by the duplicated CV and the missing explicit HACCP keyword.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with the core role: the candidate has completed butcher training, more than two years of meat-counter experience, practical beef and pork preparation experience, customer advice experience, FIFO stock rotation, and temperature-checking responsibilities. The tone also fits FreshCart’s emphasis on fresh food, honest product advice, reliability, and knowledgeable customer service. The candidate’s HACCP certificate is not currently shown in the letter, although the original candidate information confirms it. The candidate does not hold a forklift licence, which is a nice-to-have gap rather than a document defect. The candidate has not worked in a supermarket and has not used tray-sealing or self-service labelling equipment; these are experience gaps, not issues to conceal or fix through wording. The letter also does not address packaging for self-service shelves or maintaining a highly stocked counter, but the original material does not establish those experiences.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL — In the cover-letter document, delete everything from “CURRICULUM VITAE” through the end of the duplicated LANGUAGES section. Retain only the cover letter beginning with the salutation and ending with “Kind regards, Tomislav Mesarić.” A cover letter should not contain a full copy of the CV, because the duplication makes the document harder to classify and review.

CRITICAL — In the second paragraph of the cover letter, after the sentence about recording cold-room and display-counter temperatures, add a truthful sentence such as: “I hold a Basic Food Hygiene/HACCP certificate, renewed in 2024, and apply HACCP and hygiene routines in my daily work.” This directly addresses the job’s stated HACCP requirement and uses the candidate’s verified qualification.

MINOR — In the opening paragraph, change “I completed vocational butcher training and have worked in butchery and meat-counter roles since 2015” to “I hold a vocational butcher certificate and have worked in butchery and meat-counter roles since 2015.” This is more precise and aligns directly with the requirement for completed butcher training.

MINOR — In the final paragraph, replace “bring my experience and reliability to your meat-counter team” with “bring my experience in cutting, portioning, FIFO stock rotation, HACCP routines, and customer advice to your meat-counter team.” This reinforces the job’s own terminology without claiming unsupported supermarket or packaging experience.
critique.critical_issues:
1. The document labelled as a cover letter contains the entire CV before the actual letter, including the heading “CURRICULUM VITAE.” This is confusing, unnecessarily repetitive, and may interfere with document classification or AI screening. Fix: remove the duplicated CV content and retain only the cover letter.
2. The cover letter does not explicitly mention HACCP, although HACCP knowledge is a must-have requirement and the candidate’s original information confirms a Basic Food Hygiene/HACCP certificate renewed in 2024. Fix: add the verified HACCP qualification and daily HACCP/hygiene application to the second paragraph.
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- “my experience and reliability”

Dear Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Butcher / Meat Counter Assistant position at FreshCart Supermarkets’ Zagreb-Jarun store. I hold a vocational butcher certificate and have worked in butchery and meat-counter roles since 2015, combining practical meat preparation with attentive customer service.

In my current role at Mesnica Kod Ante, I break down beef and pork, bone, trim and portion meat, and prepare fresh sausages. I also rotate cold-room stock each morning using FIFO and record cold-room and display-counter temperatures twice daily. I hold a Basic Food Hygiene/HACCP certificate, renewed in 2024, and apply HACCP and hygiene routines in my daily work. At the counter, I serve around 120 customers on a Saturday and advise them on suitable cuts and cooking times. These responsibilities align closely with your need for careful stock rotation, hygiene checks and helpful, knowledgeable service.

I value the practical craft of butchery and the customer connection that comes with giving clear advice. FreshCart’s focus on fresh food and honest product guidance reflects the kind of service I aim to provide. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience in cutting, portioning, FIFO stock rotation, HACCP routines, and customer advice to your meat-counter team.

Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to discussing how my experience could contribute to the Zagreb-Jarun store.

Kind regards,
Tomislav Mesarić

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional and well targeted to the Butcher / Meat Counter Assistant role. It clearly connects the candidate’s vocational training, meat preparation, FIFO rotation, temperature logging, HACCP routines and customer service to the employer’s stated needs. The quantified example of serving around 120 customers on a Saturday adds credibility and impact. The structure is easy to read, with no unnecessary personal detail or unsupported claims. One minor opportunity is to use the job description’s exact wording for cutting and portioning fresh meat for the service counter.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter uses ATS-relevant terms supported by the candidate’s background, including “vocational butcher certificate,” “break down,” “bone,” “trim,” “portion,” “fresh sausages,” “FIFO,” “temperature,” “HACCP,” “hygiene routines,” and “customer advice.” The plain-text structure, standard greeting, short paragraphs and conventional closing should parse reliably. AI screening probability is high because the document directly demonstrates the two must-have requirements and relates the experience to the advertised duties. “Package” and self-service-shelf experience are not included, but the candidate’s original information states that they have not used tray sealers or supermarket labelling scales, so these should not be added.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is very strong. The document shows completed butcher training, more than two years of meat-counter experience, HACCP knowledge, meat cutting and portioning, customer advice, FIFO stock rotation and temperature checks. It also reflects FreshCart’s culture signals of fresh food, honest product guidance, hygiene and helpful service. The candidate’s original information indicates no forklift licence, which is only a nice-to-have and is therefore a genuine gap rather than a document defect. The candidate also has no supermarket, tray-sealer or self-service-pack experience; this is relevant background for the employer but cannot be presented as existing experience. The letter appropriately avoids claiming any of these skills.
critique.improvement_instructions: MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the second paragraph, change “I break down beef and pork, bone, trim and portion meat, and prepare fresh sausages” to “I cut, portion and prepare fresh meat for the service counter, including breaking down beef and pork, boning, trimming and making fresh sausages.” This preserves the candidate’s truthful experience while matching the advertisement’s wording more closely. MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the final paragraph, change “my experience in cutting, portioning, FIFO stock rotation, HACCP routines, and customer advice” to “my experience cutting and portioning fresh meat for the service counter, rotating stock using FIFO, recording temperature and hygiene checks, and advising customers on cuts and preparation.” This incorporates the job ad’s “temperature and hygiene checks” terminology and makes the match more explicit.
